title_en: Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of strengthening vaccine administration, ensuring vaccine quality and supply, regulating vaccination, promoting the development of the vaccine industry, safeguarding public health, and maintaining public health security.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the activities of vaccine research and development, production, distribution, vaccination, and the supervision and administration thereof within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Matters not provided for in this Law shall be governed by the provisions of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Treatment of Infectious Diseases, and other laws and administrative regulations.
For the purpose of this Law, "vaccine" means a preventive biological product used for human immunization to prevent and control the occurrence and prevalence of diseases, including vaccines covered by the immunization program and vaccines not covered by the immunization program.

Article 3 The State shall implement the strictest management system for vaccines, adhering to the principles of safety first, risk management, full-process control, scientific regulation, and social co-governance.

Article 4 The State shall adhere to the strategic and public welfare nature of vaccine products.
The State shall support basic research and applied research on vaccines, promote vaccine research and development and innovation, and incorporate the research and development, production and stockpiling of vaccines for the prevention and control of major diseases into the national strategy.
The State shall formulate development plans and industrial policies for the vaccine industry, support the development and structural optimization of the vaccine industry, encourage scaled and intensive vaccine production, and continuously improve vaccine production processes and quality levels.

Article 5 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall strengthen quality management over the entire life cycle of vaccines, and shall be responsible for the safety, efficacy and quality controllability of vaccines.
Entities and individuals engaged in vaccine research and development, production, distribution and vaccination activities shall comply with laws, regulations, rules, standards and norms, ensure that information in the whole process is truthful, accurate, complete and traceable, bear liability according to law, and accept social supervision.

Article 6 The State shall implement an immunization planning system.
Residents living within the territory of China shall have the right to receive vaccines covered by the immunization program according to law, and shall fulfill the obligation to receive such vaccines. The government shall provide vaccines covered by the immunization program to residents free of charge.
People's governments at or above the county level and the relevant departments thereof shall ensure that children of appropriate age receive vaccines covered by the immunization program. Guardians shall ensure according to law that children of appropriate age receive vaccines covered by the immunization program on time.

Article 7 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate vaccine safety work and vaccination work into the national economic and social development plans at the corresponding level, strengthen the capacity building for vaccine supervision and administration, and establish and improve the working mechanism for vaccine supervision and administration.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the vaccine supervision and administration within their respective administrative regions, and shall exercise unified leadership, organization and coordination over such work.

Article 8 The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of vaccines nationwide. The health authority of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of vaccination nationwide. Other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration related to vaccines within their respective functions and duties.
The drug regulatory authority of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of vaccines within its administrative region. The department undertaking drug regulatory functions and duties of the people's government of a city divided into districts or of a county (hereinafter referred to as the drug regulatory authority) shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of vaccines within its administrative region. The health authority of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of vaccination within its administrative region. Other relevant departments of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration related to vaccines within their respective functions and duties.

Article 9 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish departmental coordination mechanisms to coordinate the work related to vaccine supervision and administration, regularly analyze vaccine safety situations, strengthen vaccine supervision and administration, and ensure vaccine supply.

Article 10 The State shall implement an electronic traceability system for the entire process of vaccines.
The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall, together with the health authority of the State Council, formulate unified vaccine traceability standards and norms, establish a national collaborative platform for vaccine electronic traceability, integrate traceability information of the entire process of vaccine production, distribution and vaccination, and achieve vaccine traceability.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish a vaccine electronic traceability system, which shall be connected with the national collaborative platform for vaccine electronic traceability, to achieve traceability and verifiability of vaccines at the smallest packaging unit throughout the entire process of production, distribution and vaccination.
Disease prevention and control institutions and vaccination units shall truthfully record the distribution, vaccination and other information of vaccines according to law, and provide traceability information to the national collaborative platform for vaccine electronic traceability in accordance with the provisions.

Article 11 In the process of vaccine research and development, production, and testing, a biosecurity management system shall be established and improved, biosecurity risks shall be strictly controlled, biosecurity management of pathogenic microorganisms such as bacterial and viral strains shall be strengthened, the health of operators and the public shall be protected, and the use of pathogenic microorganisms such as bacterial and viral strains shall be lawful and legitimate.
Bacterial and viral strains and cell lines used in vaccine research and development, production, and testing shall have a clear history, biological characteristics, and passage number, and detailed archives shall be established to ensure that their sources are lawful, clear, and traceable; those with unknown sources shall not be used.

Article 12 People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments thereof, disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, vaccine marketing authorization holders, and vaccine industry associations shall, through activities such as National Children's Vaccination Day, regularly carry out publicity, education and popularization of vaccine safety laws and regulations and vaccination knowledge.
News media shall carry out public-interest publicity on vaccine safety laws and regulations and vaccination knowledge, and exercise public opinion supervision over violations of vaccine laws. Reports and coverage concerning vaccines shall be comprehensive, scientific, objective, and fair.

Article 13 Vaccine industry associations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, establish and improve industry norms, promote the construction of industry integrity system, and guide and supervise their members to carry out production and operation activities according to law.

Article 14 The State shall, based on factors such as disease prevalence and population immune status, formulate relevant research and development plans, allocate necessary funds, and support the research and development of new vaccines such as combination and multivalent vaccines.
The State shall organize vaccine marketing authorization holders, scientific research institutions, and medical and health institutions to conduct joint research and development of vaccines urgently needed for disease prevention and control.

Article 15 The State shall encourage vaccine marketing authorization holders to increase investment in research and development and innovation, optimize production processes, improve quality control levels, and promote technological progress in vaccines.

Article 16 Conducting clinical trials of vaccines shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council according to law.
Clinical trials of vaccines shall be conducted or organized by tertiary medical institutions or disease prevention and control institutions at or above the provincial level that meet the conditions prescribed by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and the health authority of the State Council.
The State shall encourage qualified medical institutions, disease prevention and control institutions, and others to conduct clinical trials of vaccines according to law.

Article 17 A sponsor of a vaccine clinical trial shall formulate a clinical trial protocol, establish a safety monitoring and evaluation system for the clinical trial, carefully select subjects, reasonably set subject groups and age groups, and take effective measures based on the degree of risk to protect the lawful rights and interests of subjects.

Article 18 For conducting clinical trials of vaccines, written informed consent shall be obtained from the subject; if the subject is a person with no capacity for civil conduct, written informed consent shall be obtained from his or her guardian; if the subject is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, written informed consent shall be obtained from both the subject and his or her guardian.

Article 19 Vaccines to be marketed in China shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and obtain drug registration certificates; for applying for vaccine registration, truthful, sufficient and reliable data, materials and samples shall be provided.
For vaccines urgently needed for disease prevention and control and innovative vaccines, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall give priority to review and approval.

Article 20 For vaccines urgently needed for responding to major public health emergencies or other vaccines deemed urgently needed by the health authority of the State Council, if the benefits are evaluated as outweighing the risks, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council may conditionally approve the vaccine registration application.
In the event of an exceptionally major public health emergency or other emergency seriously threatening public health, the health authority of the State Council may, based on the needs of infectious disease prevention and control, make a proposal for emergency use of vaccines, and after demonstration and consent by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council, the vaccines may be used urgently within a certain scope and period.

Article 21 When approving a vaccine registration application, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall approve the production process, quality control standards, instructions and labels of the vaccine.
The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall promptly publish the contents of vaccine instructions and labels on its website.

Article 22 The State shall implement a strict access system for vaccine production.
Engaging in vaccine production activities shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the people's government at or above the provincial level, and a drug production license shall be obtained.
Engaging in vaccine production activities shall, in addition to meeting the conditions for engaging in drug production activities as prescribed in the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, meet the following conditions:
(1) Having an appropriate scale and sufficient production capacity reserves;
(2) Having systems, facilities and equipment for ensuring biosafety; and
(3) Meeting the needs of disease prevention and control.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall have the capacity for vaccine production; if it is truly necessary to commission production beyond its own vaccine production capacity, it shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council. The entity accepting commissioned production shall comply with the provisions of this Law and relevant state regulations, and shall ensure vaccine quality.

Article 23 The legal representative and principal responsible person of a vaccine marketing authorization holder shall have a good credit record, and key position personnel such as the person in charge of production management, the person in charge of quality management, and the authorized person for quality shall have relevant professional background and work experience.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall strengthen the training and assessment of the personnel specified in the preceding paragraph, and shall promptly report their appointment and changes to the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 24 Vaccines shall be produced and tested in accordance with the approved production processes and quality control standards, and the entire production process shall comply with the requirements of the Good Manufacturing Practice for drugs.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall, in accordance with the provisions, review and test the entire vaccine production process and vaccine quality.

Article 25 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish a complete production quality management system, continuously strengthen deviation management, adopt information technology means to truthfully record all data generated in the production and testing process, and ensure that the entire production process continuously meets statutory requirements.

Article 26 The State shall implement a vaccine lot release system.
Before each batch of vaccines is marketed or imported, it shall be reviewed and tested by a lot release institution designated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council in accordance with relevant technical requirements. If it meets the requirements, a lot release certificate shall be issued; if it does not, a notice of non-issuance of lot release certificate shall be issued.
Vaccines for which lot release is not granted shall not be marketed, and shall be destroyed under the supervision of the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government; imported vaccines for which lot release is not granted shall be destroyed under the supervision of the drug regulatory authority of the port location or otherwise disposed of according to law.
The drug regulatory authority of the State Council and the lot release institution shall promptly publish the lot release results of marketed vaccines for public inquiry.

Article 27 For applying for vaccine lot release, the applicant shall, in accordance with the provisions, provide the lot release institution with materials such as summaries of batch production and testing records, and samples such as products of the same batch number. For imported vaccines, the applicant shall also provide the certificate of origin and the lot release certificate; if lot release is exempted in the country of origin, the certificate of exemption from lot release shall be provided.

Article 28 Vaccines urgently needed for preventing and controlling infectious disease epidemics or responding to emergencies may be exempted from lot release upon approval by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 29 Vaccine lot release shall be carried out batch by batch through document review and sample testing. The testing items and testing frequency for vaccine lot release shall be dynamically adjusted based on the risk assessment of vaccine quality.
If there is a doubt about the authenticity of the application documents or samples for vaccine lot release, or if there are other circumstances requiring further verification, the lot release institution shall verify them, and if necessary, shall organize on-site verification by means such as on-site sample testing.

Article 30 If, during the lot release process, a lot release institution discovers that a vaccine has a significant quality risk, it shall promptly report to the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
The department that receives the report shall immediately conduct an on-site inspection of the vaccine marketing authorization holder, and based on the inspection results, notify the lot release institution to refuse lot release or suspend lot release for the relevant products or all products of the vaccine marketing authorization holder, and order the vaccine marketing authorization holder to rectify. The vaccine marketing authorization holder shall rectify immediately and promptly report the rectification to the department that ordered the rectification.

Article 31 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall truthfully record deviations in production processes, quality differences, faults and accidents during production, and the measures taken, and shall specify them in the documents for applying for lot release of the corresponding batch of products; if the vaccine quality may be affected, the vaccine marketing authorization holder shall immediately take measures and report to the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 32 Vaccines covered by the national immunization program shall be subject to centralized bidding or unified negotiation organized by the health authority of the State Council together with the finance authority of the State Council and others, and the bid-winning prices or transaction prices shall be determined and announced, and provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall implement unified procurement.
Immunization program vaccines other than those covered by the national immunization program and vaccines not covered by the immunization program shall be procured by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government through provincial public resource trading platforms.

Article 33 The price of a vaccine shall be independently and reasonably set by the vaccine marketing authorization holder according to law. The price level, price difference rate, and profit margin of vaccines shall be maintained within a reasonable range.

Article 34 A provincial disease prevention and control institution shall, based on the national immunization program and the needs of disease prevention and control in its administrative region, formulate a plan for the use of immunization program vaccines in its administrative region, report it to the department that organizes vaccine procurement in accordance with relevant state regulations, and at the same time file it with the health authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 35 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall supply vaccines to disease prevention and control institutions in accordance with the procurement contract.
Disease prevention and control institutions shall supply vaccines to vaccination units in accordance with the provisions.
No entity or individual other than a disease prevention and control institution may supply vaccines to vaccination units, and vaccination units shall not accept such vaccines.

Article 36 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall deliver vaccines to disease prevention and control institutions or vaccination units designated by such institutions in accordance with the procurement contract.
If a vaccine marketing authorization holder or a disease prevention and control institution delivers vaccines by itself, it shall have the conditions for cold chain storage and transportation of vaccines; it may also entrust a qualified vaccine delivery unit to deliver vaccines.
A disease prevention and control institution may charge storage and transportation fees for delivering vaccines not covered by the immunization program. The specific measures shall be formulated by the finance authority of the State Council together with the price authority of the State Council, and the charging standards shall be formulated by the price authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government together with the finance authority.

Article 37 Disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, vaccine marketing authorization holders, and vaccine delivery units shall comply with the norms for vaccine storage and transportation management to ensure vaccine quality.
During the entire process of storage and transportation, vaccines shall be kept in the prescribed temperature environment, cold chain storage and transportation shall meet the requirements, and the temperature shall be monitored and recorded at regular intervals.
The norms for vaccine storage and transportation management shall be jointly formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and the health authority of the State Council.

Article 38 When selling vaccines, a vaccine marketing authorization holder shall provide a copy or electronic document of the lot release certificate affixed with its seal; for selling imported vaccines, it shall also provide a copy or electronic document of the import drug customs clearance form affixed with its seal.
When receiving or purchasing vaccines, a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit shall request the certification documents specified in the preceding paragraph, and shall keep them for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference.

Article 39 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall, in accordance with the provisions, establish truthful, accurate and complete sales records, and keep them for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference.
Disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, and vaccine delivery units shall, in accordance with the provisions, establish truthful, accurate and complete records of receipt, purchase, storage, delivery, and supply, and keep them for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference.
When receiving or purchasing vaccines, a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit shall request the temperature monitoring records for the entire process of the current transportation and storage, and keep them for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference; if the temperature monitoring records for the entire process of the current transportation and storage cannot be provided, or the temperature control does not meet the requirements, the vaccines shall not be received or purchased, and the matter shall be immediately reported to the drug regulatory authority and the health authority of the local people's government at or above the county level.

Article 40 Disease prevention and control institutions and vaccination units shall establish a regular vaccine inspection system, take measures such as isolated storage and setting up warning signs for vaccines with problems such as unidentifiable packaging, storage temperature not meeting requirements, or exceeding the validity period, and dispose of them in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory authority, the health authority, and the ecological environment authority of the State Council. Disease prevention and control institutions and vaccination units shall truthfully record the disposal situation, and the disposal records shall be kept for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference.

Article 41 The health authority of the State Council shall formulate the national immunization program; the types of vaccines covered by the national immunization program shall be drafted by the health authority of the State Council together with the finance authority of the State Council, and shall be published after being approved by the State Council.
The health authority of the State Council shall establish a national immunization program expert advisory committee, and shall, together with the finance authority of the State Council, establish a mechanism for dynamic adjustment of the types of vaccines covered by the national immunization program.
When implementing the national immunization program, the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the needs of disease prevention and control in their administrative regions, add types of vaccines covered by the immunization program, and shall report them to the health authority of the State Council for filing and publish them.

Article 42 The health authority of the State Council shall formulate and publish the work norms for vaccination, and strengthen the standardized management of vaccination.
The health authority of the State Council shall formulate and publish the immunization schedule for vaccines covered by the national immunization program and the guiding principles for the use of vaccines not covered by the immunization program.
The health authority of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall formulate vaccination plans based on the actual conditions of its administrative region, and report them to the health authority of the State Council for filing.

Article 43 Disease prevention and control institutions at all levels shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, carry out work related to vaccination, including publicity, training, technical guidance, monitoring, evaluation, epidemiological investigation, and emergency response.

Article 44 A vaccination unit shall meet the following conditions:
(1) Having obtained a medical institution practice license;
(2) Having physicians, nurses, or village doctors who have received professional training on vaccination organized by the health authority of the people's government of the county level and have passed the assessment;
(3) Having cold storage facilities, equipment and a cold storage management system that comply with the norms for vaccine storage and transportation management.
The health authority of the local people's government at or above the county level shall designate qualified medical institutions to undertake the work of administering vaccines covered by the immunization program within the responsible area. Qualified medical institutions may undertake the work of administering vaccines not covered by the immunization program, and shall report to the health authority that issued their medical institution practice license for filing.
A vaccination unit shall strengthen internal management, and shall comply with the work norms for vaccination, the immunization schedule, the guiding principles for the use of vaccines, and the vaccination plans when carrying out vaccination work.
Disease prevention and control institutions at all levels shall strengthen technical guidance on vaccination work and management of vaccine use for vaccination units.

Article 45 When administering vaccination, a medical and health professional shall inform the recipient or his or her guardian of the type, efficacy, contraindications, adverse reactions, and matters needing attention such as on-site observation of the vaccine to be administered, inquire about the recipient's health status and whether there are any contraindications to vaccination, and truthfully record the information provided and the inquiries made. The recipient or his or her guardian shall truthfully provide information on the recipient's health status and contraindications to vaccination. If the recipient cannot be vaccinated due to contraindications, the medical and health professional shall provide medical advice to the recipient or his or her guardian, and truthfully record the provision of such advice.
Before administering vaccination, a medical and health professional shall, in accordance with the requirements of the work norms for vaccination, check the recipient's health status, verify contraindications to vaccination, check the vaccination certificate, inspect the appearance, batch number, and expiry date of the vaccine and the syringe, and verify the recipient's name, age, and the name, specification, dosage, injection site, and injection route of the vaccine, ensuring that the recipient, the vaccination certificate, and the vaccine information are consistent, and only after confirming that there is no error may the vaccination be administered.
A medical and health professional shall administer vaccination to recipients who meet the vaccination conditions. If a recipient experiences adverse reactions during the on-site observation period, the medical and health professional shall promptly take measures such as treatment in accordance with the requirements of the work norms for vaccination.

Article 46 A medical and health professional shall, in accordance with the provisions of the health authority of the State Council, truthfully, accurately and completely record vaccination information such as the type of vaccine, the marketing authorization holder, the identification information of the smallest packaging unit, the expiry date, the time of vaccination, the medical and health professional who administered the vaccination, and the recipient, to ensure that the vaccination information is traceable and queryable. The vaccination records shall be kept for not less than five years after the expiry of the vaccine validity period for future reference.

Article 47 The State shall implement a vaccination certificate system for children. Within one month after the birth of a child, his or her guardian shall go to the vaccination unit responsible for vaccination in the child's place of residence or the hospital of birth to obtain a vaccination certificate for the child. The vaccination unit or the hospital of birth shall not refuse to issue the certificate. The guardian shall properly keep the vaccination certificate.
Vaccination shall be managed on the basis of the place of residence. During the period when a child leaves the original place of residence, the vaccination unit responsible for vaccination in the current place of residence shall be responsible for administering vaccination to the child.
The format of the vaccination certificate shall be prescribed by the health authority of the State Council.

Article 48 When a child enters a nursery, kindergarten or school, the nursery, kindergarten or school shall check the vaccination certificate; if it is found that the child has not received vaccines covered by the immunization program in accordance with the provisions, it shall report to the vaccination unit responsible for vaccination in the child's place of residence or the place where the nursery, kindergarten or school is located, and cooperate with the vaccination unit to urge the guardian of the child to get the child vaccinated as required. Disease prevention and control institutions shall provide technical guidance for nursery, kindergarten and school in checking vaccination certificates.
The measures for checking vaccination certificates for children entering nursery, kindergarten or school shall be formulated by the health authority of the State Council together with the education administration department of the State Council.

Article 49 A vaccination unit shall not charge any fee for administering vaccines covered by the immunization program.
For administering vaccines not covered by the immunization program, a vaccination unit may, in addition to the vaccine fee, charge a vaccination service fee. The charging standards for the vaccination service fee shall be formulated by the price authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government together with the finance authority.

Article 50 The health authority of a local people's government at or above the county level may, based on information from infectious disease surveillance and early warning, and for the purpose of preventing and controlling the outbreak or prevalence of infectious diseases, submit a report to the people's government at the same level for a decision, and file it with the health authority of the people's government at or above the provincial level, and may carry out group vaccination within its administrative region.
If group vaccination needs to be carried out nationwide or across provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, it shall be decided by the health authority of the State Council.
The local people's government at or above the county level or the health authority of the State Council that makes the decision on group vaccination shall organize relevant departments to do a good job in personnel training, publicity and education, and material allocation.
No entity or individual may carry out group vaccination without authorization.

Article 51 When an infectious disease breaks out or becomes epidemic, if the local people's government at or above the county level or its health department needs to take emergency vaccination measures, such measures shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 53 The State shall strengthen the monitoring of adverse events following immunization. The monitoring plan for adverse events following immunization shall be formulated by the health department of the State Council jointly with the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 54 When a vaccination unit, medical institution, or the like discovers a suspected adverse event following immunization, it shall report it to the disease prevention and control institution in accordance with regulations.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish a dedicated unit, assign full-time personnel, proactively collect, track, and analyze suspected adverse events following immunization, take timely risk control measures, report suspected adverse events following immunization to the disease prevention and control institution, and submit a quality analysis report to the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 55 For a suspected adverse event following immunization, the disease prevention and control institution shall promptly report it in accordance with regulations, organize investigation and diagnosis, and inform the recipient or the recipient's guardian of the investigation and diagnosis conclusions. If there is a dispute over the investigation and diagnosis conclusions, an expert evaluation may be applied for in accordance with the evaluation methods formulated by the health department of the State Council.
Where a suspected adverse event following immunization has a significant social impact, such as the death or severe disability of the recipient caused by vaccination, or a cluster of suspected adverse events following immunization, the health department and the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the city divided into districts shall organize investigation and handling in accordance with their respective responsibilities.

Article 56 The State shall implement a compensation system for adverse events following immunization. If, during or after vaccination, the recipient suffers death, severe disability, organ or tissue damage, or other harm that is determined to be or cannot be ruled out as an adverse event following immunization, compensation shall be provided. The scope of compensation shall be managed by a catalogue and dynamically adjusted based on actual circumstances.
Compensation expenses required for the administration of vaccines under the immunization program shall be arranged by the finance department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government from the vaccination funds; compensation expenses required for the administration of vaccines not under the immunization program shall be borne by the relevant vaccine marketing authorization holder. The State encourages the use of commercial insurance and other forms of compensation for recipients of adverse events following immunization.
Compensation for adverse events following immunization shall be timely, convenient, and reasonable. The scope, standards, and procedures for compensation for adverse events following immunization shall be stipulated by the State Council, and the specific implementation measures shall be formulated by the provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 57 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish and improve a vaccine quality management system covering the entire life cycle, formulate and implement a post-marketing risk management plan for the vaccine, conduct post-marketing studies of the vaccine, and further confirm the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of the vaccine.
For a vaccine for which further research requirements were imposed at the time of approval of its registration application, the vaccine marketing authorization holder shall complete the research within the prescribed period; if the research is not completed within the time limit or it cannot be proved that the benefits outweigh the risks, the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall handle the matter according to law, up to revoking the drug registration certificate of the vaccine.

Article 58 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall conduct quality tracking and analysis of the vaccine, continuously improve quality control standards, refine production processes, and enhance the stability of the production process.
If changes occur in the production process, production site, key equipment, or the like, assessment and validation shall be carried out, and the changes shall be filed or reported in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory department of the State Council on change management; if the changes may affect the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of the vaccine, approval from the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be obtained.

Article 59 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall continuously update the package insert and label based on post-marketing studies, adverse events following immunization, and other circumstances, and shall apply for approval or filing in accordance with regulations.
The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall promptly publish the updated content of the vaccine package insert and label on its website.

Article 60 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish a system for vaccine quality review analysis and risk reporting, and shall truthfully report to the drug regulatory department of the State Council each year in accordance with regulations on the vaccine's production and distribution, post-marketing studies, risk management, and other relevant circumstances.

Article 61 The drug regulatory department of the State Council may, based on actual circumstances, order a vaccine marketing authorization holder to conduct a post-marketing evaluation, or directly organize and conduct a post-marketing evaluation.
For a vaccine that causes serious adverse events following immunization or harms human health for other reasons, the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall revoke the drug registration certificate of that vaccine.

Article 62 The drug regulatory department of the State Council may, based on the needs of disease prevention and control and the development of the vaccine industry, organize post-marketing evaluations of vaccine varieties. If it finds that the product design, production process, safety, efficacy, or quality controllability of a vaccine variety is significantly inferior to other vaccine varieties for preventing and controlling the same disease, it shall revoke the drug registration certificates of all vaccines of that variety and abolish the corresponding national drug standards.

Article 63 People's governments at or above the county level shall include the necessary funds for vaccine safety, the purchase of vaccines under the immunization program, vaccination work, and information technology construction, among others, in their respective government budgets, and shall ensure the implementation of the immunization program system.
The county people's government shall provide subsidies to rural doctors and other primary medical and health personnel engaged in vaccination work in accordance with relevant state regulations.
The State shall provide support to economically underdeveloped areas for vaccination work as needed. The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government and the people's governments of cities divided into districts shall provide necessary financial subsidies to the people's governments of economically underdeveloped counties for carrying out work related to vaccination.

Article 64 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, based on the epidemic trends of infectious diseases in their respective administrative regions and within the scope of the disease prevention and control projects determined by the health department of the State Council, determine the projects related to vaccination in their administrative regions and ensure the implementation of such projects.

Article 65 The health department of the State Council shall, based on the usage plans for vaccines under the national immunization program of each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government, provide the vaccine marketing authorization holders with demand information for vaccines under the national immunization program, and the vaccine marketing authorization holders shall reasonably arrange production based on the vaccine demand information.
When there is a risk of vaccine supply shortage, the health department of the State Council and the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall make recommendations, and the competent industry and information technology department of the State Council and the finance department of the State Council shall take effective measures to ensure vaccine production and supply.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall organize production according to law and ensure vaccine supply; if a vaccine marketing authorization holder ceases vaccine production, it shall promptly report to the drug regulatory department of the State Council or the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 66 The State shall include vaccines in its strategic material reserves, implementing a two-level reserve system at the central and provincial levels.
The competent industry and information technology department of the State Council and the finance department of the State Council, together with the health department, public security department, market supervision and administration department, and drug regulatory department of the State Council, shall, based on the needs of disease prevention, control, and public health emergency preparedness, strengthen the management of the production capacity and products of reserved vaccines, and establish a dynamic adjustment mechanism.

Article 67 Funds allocated by governments at all levels for vaccination shall be used exclusively for that purpose, and no unit or individual may misappropriate or divert such funds.
Relevant units and individuals that use vaccination funds shall, according to law, accept audit supervision by audit authorities.

Article 68 The State shall implement a compulsory vaccine liability insurance system.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall take out compulsory vaccine liability insurance in accordance with regulations. If a recipient suffers harm due to a vaccine quality problem, the insurance company shall pay compensation within the liability limit covered by the insurance.
The specific implementation measures for the compulsory vaccine liability insurance system shall be formulated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the health department of the State Council, the insurance regulatory authority, and others.

Article 69 When an infectious disease breaks out or becomes epidemic, the relevant vaccine marketing authorization holders shall promptly produce and supply vaccines to prevent and control the infectious disease. Transportation units shall give priority to the transport of vaccines for preventing and controlling infectious diseases. People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall properly organize, coordinate, and ensure such work.

Article 70 The drug regulatory department and the health department shall supervise and manage the entire process of vaccine development, production, distribution, and vaccination in accordance with their respective responsibilities, and shall supervise vaccine marketing authorization holders, disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, and other entities to perform their obligations according to law.
The drug regulatory department shall, according to law, conduct supervision and inspection of vaccine quality during vaccine development, production, storage, transportation, and vaccination. The health department shall, according to law, conduct supervision and inspection of the implementation of the immunization program system and vaccination activities.
The drug regulatory department shall strengthen on-site inspections of vaccine marketing authorization holders; when necessary, it may conduct extended inspections of units and individuals that provide products or services for vaccine development, production, distribution, and other activities; the relevant units and individuals shall cooperate and shall not refuse or conceal information.

Article 71 The State shall build a professional and specialized team of drug inspectors at the central and provincial levels to strengthen the supervision and inspection of vaccines.
The drug regulatory department of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall select and station inspectors at the premises of vaccine marketing authorization holders. The inspectors shall be responsible for supervising and inspecting the implementation of the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for drugs, collecting clues about vaccine quality risks and illegal or non-compliant acts, reporting the situation to the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and making recommendations, and shall be accountable for their conduct during the stationing period.

Article 72 If there is a potential safety hazard in vaccine quality management and the vaccine marketing authorization holder fails to take timely measures to eliminate it, the drug regulatory department may take measures such as conducting a responsible interview or ordering rectification within a specified time limit.
If there is a serious violation of the relevant drug quality management standards, the drug regulatory department shall order the suspension of vaccine production, sales, and distribution and immediate rectification; after the rectification is completed and the drug regulatory department has verified compliance through inspection, production, sales, and distribution may be resumed.
The drug regulatory department shall establish a credit record system for vaccine marketing authorization holders and their relevant personnel, include the records in the national credit information sharing platform, publish information on serious breaches of trust in accordance with regulations, and implement joint disciplinary actions.

Article 73 If a vaccine has or is suspected of having a quality problem, the vaccine marketing authorization holder, disease prevention and control institution, and vaccination unit shall immediately stop sales, distribution, and use, and if necessary, immediately stop production, and shall report to the drug regulatory department and the health department of the people's government at or above the county level in accordance with regulations. The health department shall immediately organize the disease prevention and control institution and vaccination unit to take necessary emergency response measures, and at the same time report to the health department of the higher-level people's government. The drug regulatory department shall, according to law, take measures such as sealing up and seizing. For vaccines that have already been sold, the vaccine marketing authorization holder shall promptly notify the relevant disease prevention and control institutions, vaccine distribution units, and vaccination units, and shall recall the vaccines in accordance with regulations, truthfully recording the recall and notification, and the disease prevention and control institutions, vaccine distribution units, and vaccination units shall cooperate.
If the production, sale, distribution, use, or recall of a vaccine is not stopped in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the drug regulatory department and the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall, in accordance with their respective responsibilities, order the cessation of production, sale, distribution, use, or recall of the vaccine.
If a vaccine marketing authorization holder, disease prevention and control institution, or vaccination unit discovers a vaccine that has or is suspected of having a quality problem, it shall not conceal, make false reports, delay reporting, omit reporting, or conceal, forge, or destroy relevant evidence.

Article 74 A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall establish an information disclosure system, and shall promptly disclose on its website in accordance with regulations information such as vaccine product information, package inserts and labels, the implementation status of relevant drug quality management standards, lot release, recall, inspection and penalty history, and the status of compulsory vaccine liability insurance, among others.

Article 75 The drug regulatory department of the State Council, together with the health department of the State Council and others, shall establish an information sharing mechanism for vaccine quality, vaccination, and other matters.
The drug regulatory departments and health departments of people's governments at or above the provincial level shall, following the principles of being scientific, objective, timely, and open, organize vaccine marketing authorization holders, disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, news media, scientific research institutions, and others to exchange and communicate information on vaccine quality and vaccination.

Article 76 The State shall implement a unified vaccine safety information disclosure system.
Vaccine safety risk warning information, major vaccine safety incidents and their investigation and handling information, and other vaccine safety information determined by the State Council to be disclosed uniformly shall be disclosed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments. The national report on adverse events following immunization shall be disclosed uniformly by the health department of the State Council jointly with the drug regulatory department of the State Council. The above information shall not be released without authorization. Major vaccine safety information shall be disclosed in a timely, accurate, and comprehensive manner, and shall be scientifically evaluated and necessary explanations given in accordance with regulations.
If a drug regulatory department of a people's government at or above the county level discovers vaccine safety information that may mislead the public and public opinion, it shall immediately verify and analyze the information jointly with the health department and other relevant departments, professional institutions, and relevant vaccine marketing authorization holders, and promptly disclose the results.
No unit or individual may fabricate or disseminate false vaccine safety information.

Article 77 Any unit or individual has the right to know vaccine information according to law and to provide opinions and suggestions on vaccine supervision and management work.
Any unit or individual has the right to report to the health department, drug regulatory department, or other departments about illegal acts related to vaccines, and has the right to report to the people's government at the same level or the higher level, its relevant departments, or supervisory authorities about the failure of the health department, drug regulatory department, or other departments and their staff to perform their supervision and management duties according to law. The relevant departments and authorities shall promptly verify and handle such reports; if a report is verified to be true, the whistleblower shall be rewarded in accordance with regulations; if a whistleblower reports serious illegal acts of the unit in which the whistleblower works and the report is verified to be true, a substantial reward shall be given.

Article 78 People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate emergency response plans for vaccine safety incidents, providing for the classification of vaccine safety incidents, the organizational command structure and responsibilities for handling, the prevention and early warning mechanism, the handling procedures, and emergency support measures, among others.
A vaccine marketing authorization holder shall formulate a vaccine safety incident handling plan, regularly inspect the implementation of various preventive measures, and promptly eliminate potential safety hazards.
When a vaccine safety incident occurs, the vaccine marketing authorization holder shall immediately report to the drug regulatory department of the State Council or the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government; disease prevention and control institutions, vaccination units, and medical institutions shall immediately report to the health department and the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the county level. The drug regulatory department shall, jointly with the health department and in accordance with the provisions of the emergency response plan, establish a command body for handling the vaccine safety incident, carry out medical treatment, risk control, investigation and handling, information release, explanations, and other work, and properly handle post-event matters such as catch-up vaccination. The costs of catch-up vaccination for a vaccine safety incident caused by quality problems shall be borne by the vaccine marketing authorization holder.
Relevant units and individuals shall not conceal, make false reports, delay reporting, or omit reporting of vaccine safety incidents, and shall not conceal, forge, or destroy relevant evidence.
Article 79 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law and constitutes a crime shall be investigated for criminal liability with heavier punishment according to law.

Article 80 If a vaccine produced or sold is a counterfeit drug, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall confiscate the illegal income, the illegally produced or sold vaccine, and items such as raw materials, excipients, packaging materials, and equipment specifically used for the illegal production of the vaccine, order the suspension of production or business for rectification, revoke the drug registration certificate and up to the drug manufacturing license, and impose a fine of not less than fifteen times but not more than fifty times the value of the illegally produced or sold vaccine; if the value is less than 500,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 500,000 yuan.
If a vaccine produced or sold is a substandard drug, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall confiscate the illegal income, the illegally produced or sold vaccine, and items such as raw materials, excipients, packaging materials, and equipment specifically used for the illegal production of the vaccine, order the suspension of production or business for rectification, and impose a fine of not less than ten times but not more than thirty times the value of the illegally produced or sold vaccine; if the value is less than 500,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the drug registration certificate and up to the drug manufacturing license shall be revoked.
If the vaccine produced or sold is a counterfeit drug, or if the vaccine produced or sold is a substandard drug and the circumstances are serious, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall confiscate the income earned from the unit during the period of the illegal act from the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, key position personnel, and other responsible persons, impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the income earned, permanently prohibit them from engaging in drug production and business activities, and the public security organ shall impose detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days.

Article 82 Except as otherwise provided in this Law, if a vaccine marketing authorization holder or other unit violates the relevant drug quality management standards, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and give a warning; if the unit refuses to rectify, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 3,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, the unit shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification, and up to the relevant drug approval certificates and drug manufacturing license shall be revoked, and the income earned from the unit during the period of the illegal act shall be confiscated from the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, key position personnel, and other responsible persons, and a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the income earned shall be imposed, and they shall be prohibited from engaging in drug production and business activities for up to ten years or permanently.

Article 85 If a disease prevention and control institution, vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit violates the cold chain storage and transportation requirements of the vaccine storage and transportation management standards, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, give a warning, destroy the illegally stored or transported vaccine, and confiscate the illegal income; if the unit refuses to rectify, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed on the vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than ten times but not more than thirty times the value of the illegally stored or transported vaccine shall be imposed on the vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit; if the value is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan, and the vaccine marketing authorization holder or vaccine distribution unit shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification, up to revoking the relevant drug approval certificates and drug manufacturing license, and the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, key position personnel, and other responsible persons of the vaccine marketing authorization holder or vaccine distribution unit shall be punished in accordance with Article 82 of this Law.
If a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit commits the illegal act specified in the preceding paragraph, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall give a warning up to removal from office to the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons according to law, and order the responsible medical and health personnel to suspend their practice for not less than one year but not more than eighteen months; if serious consequences are caused, the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons shall be given dismissal according to law, and the vaccination qualification of the vaccination unit may be revoked, and the original issuing department shall revoke the practice certificate of the responsible medical and health personnel.

Article 86 If a disease prevention and control institution, vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit commits an act that violates the vaccine storage and transportation management standards other than those specified in Article 85 of this Law, the drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal income; if the unit refuses to rectify, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan shall be imposed on the vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than three times but not more than ten times the value of the illegally stored or transported vaccine shall be imposed on the vaccination unit, vaccine marketing authorization holder, or vaccine distribution unit; if the value is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan.
If a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit commits the illegal act specified in the preceding paragraph, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level may give a warning up to removal from office to the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons according to law, and order the responsible medical and health personnel to suspend their practice for not less than six months but not more than one year; if serious consequences are caused, the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons shall be given dismissal according to law, and the original issuing department shall revoke the practice certificate of the responsible medical and health personnel.

Article 89 If a disease prevention and control institution, vaccination unit, or medical institution fails to report suspected adverse events following immunization or vaccine safety incidents in accordance with regulations, or fails to organize investigation or diagnosis of suspected adverse events following immunization in accordance with regulations, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and give a warning; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed on the vaccination unit or medical institution, and the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons of the disease prevention and control institution, vaccination unit, or medical institution shall be given a warning up to removal from office according to law; if serious consequences are caused, the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons shall be given dismissal according to law, and the original issuing department shall revoke the practice certificate of the responsible medical and health personnel.

Article 90 If a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit collects fees in violation of the provisions of this Law, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall supervise the return of the illegally collected fees to the unit or individual that originally paid them, and the market supervision and administration department of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 91 In violation of the provisions of this Law, if a unit or individual, without being designated by the health department of the local people's government at or above the county level, engages in the administration of vaccines under the immunization program, or engages in the administration of vaccines not under the immunization program without meeting the conditions or without filing, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, give a warning, confiscate the illegal income and the illegally held vaccines, order the suspension of business for rectification, and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan, and shall impose a sanction on the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons according to law.
In violation of the provisions of this Law, if a unit or individual other than a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit conducts mass vaccination without authorization, the health department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, confiscate the illegal income and the illegally held vaccines, and impose a fine of not less than ten times but not more than thirty times the value of the illegally held vaccines; if the value is less than 50,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 50,000 yuan.

Article 92 If a guardian fails to ensure that a child of appropriate age receives the vaccines under the immunization program on time according to law, the health department of the county people's government shall give criticism and education, and order rectification.
If a nursery, kindergarten, or school fails to check the vaccination certificate in accordance with regulations when a child enters the institution or school, or fails to report to the vaccination unit after discovering a child who has not been vaccinated in accordance with regulations, the education administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, give a warning, and impose a sanction on the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 93 If a person fabricates or disseminates false vaccine safety information, or creates a disturbance at a vaccination unit, constituting a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty according to law.
If a communication medium such as a newspaper, periodical, radio station, television station, or website fabricates or disseminates false vaccine safety information, the relevant department shall impose a penalty according to law, and impose a sanction on the principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 96 If a recipient suffers harm due to a vaccine quality problem, the vaccine marketing authorization holder shall bear compensation liability according to law.
If a disease prevention and control institution or vaccination unit causes harm to a recipient due to violation of vaccination work standards, immunization procedures, vaccine use guidelines, or vaccination protocols, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 97 For the purposes of this Law, the meanings of the following terms are:
"Vaccines under the immunization program" refer to vaccines that residents shall receive in accordance with government regulations, including vaccines determined by the national immunization program, vaccines added by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government when implementing the national immunization program, and vaccines used in emergency vaccinations or mass vaccinations organized by the people's government at or above the county level or its health department.
"Vaccines not under the immunization program" refer to other vaccines that residents voluntarily receive.
"Vaccine marketing authorization holder" refers to an enterprise that has obtained a vaccine drug registration certificate and a drug manufacturing license according to law.

Article 98 The State encourages vaccine manufacturers to produce and export vaccines in accordance with international procurement requirements.
Exported vaccines shall meet the standards of the importing country (region) or the contract requirements.

Article 99 Entry-exit vaccination and the procurement of vaccines required therefor shall be separately stipulated by the border health and quarantine authority after consultation with the finance department of the State Council.
Article 100 This Law shall come into force as of December 1, 2019.
